_provenance.note: Colorado citation authorities. Colorado maintains a single primary citation family — 10 CCR 2506-1 (Code of Colorado Regulations, RULE MANUAL VOLUME 4, SNAP), cited by section number and decimal sub-part, e.g. '10 CCR 2506-1-4.206', '10 CCR 2506-1-4.407.1'. This is Colorado's OWN official citation format (used identically by the Secretary of State, Cornell Law's LII, and Justia) — unlike most of this roster's other states, this pack does not need to invent a short prefix, because Colorado's formally-promulgated regulation IS the manual (see the manual-structure supplement). Colorado's own statute citations use the standard form 'C.R.S. § 26-2-###'.

patterns.note: Colorado's Code of Colorado Regulations, Rule Manual Volume 4, SNAP, cited by section and optional decimal sub-part, e.g. 4.206 (Categories of Eligibility), 4.311 (ABAWD Work Requirements), 4.407.1 (Standard Deduction).
Colorado Revised Statutes, Title 26 (Human Services Code), Article 2 (Public Assistance), Part 3 (Food Stamps), e.g. § 26-2-305 (Fraudulent acts; drug-related felony disqualification).

coccr.note: SNAP Definitions — incl. Able-Bodied Adult Without Dependents, Basic/Expanded Categorical Eligibility, Basic Utility Allowance
Processing Standards for Expedited Service — plain federal criteria (gross income under $150, liquid resources $100 or less) and 7-calendar-day ceiling

Categories of Eligibility — Basic Categorical Eligibility (BCE), Expanded Categorical Eligibility (ECE) at 200% FPL, and Standard Eligibility (SE); the drug-related-felony BCE/ECE disqualification carve-out at 4.206(C)(1)(c)/(C)(2)(c)/(C)(3)(a)(2)

Newly-Certified and Ongoing Households; Initial Month Allotment Prorating; Benefit Allotment formula (net income x 30%, subtracted from the max allotment) and the maximum/minimum monthly allotment tables. NOT independently reconfirmed for FFY2026 — the regulation's own tables are labeled 'Effective October 1, 2024' — see PROVENANCE.md
Certification Periods — general rules; longest predictable period assigned
Certification Period Guidelines — 24-month period for all-60+/disabled no-earned-income households (12-month periodic report required); 6-month period for all other households

ABAWD Work Requirements — header reads '[Effective 1/4/2025]' but text still recites the pre-OBBBA 18-54 age range and now-federally-removed homelessness/veteran/foster-care exemptions. NOT current — contradicts CDHS's own dedicated ABAWD FAQ page and February 2026 desk aid, both stating 18-64. See PROVENANCE.md
Household Income Eligibility — prospective budgeting, income conversion and averaging rules

Deductions and Exclusions from Income — header reads '[Effective 1/4/2025]'; lists the five allowable deductions (standard, earned income, excess shelter, dependent care, excess medical) and the child support income exclusion at 4.407(D)

Standard Deduction — computed as 8.31% of the federal poverty guideline by household size; dollar figures labeled 'Effective October 1, 2024' (FFY2025), NOT independently reconfirmed for FFY2026 — see PROVENANCE.md
Excess Shelter Deduction — cap for households without an elderly/disabled member; Homeless Shelter Deduction estimate; allowable shelter cost categories

Four-Tiered Mandatory Standard Utility Allowance — HCUA, BUA, OUA, and Telephone Allowance; all four dollar figures labeled 'Effective October 1, 2024' (FFY2025), NOT independently reconfirmed for FFY2026 — see PROVENANCE.md
Child Support Expense Exclusion — legally binding child support is an income exclusion applied before the gross income test, not an ordinary post-gross deduction

Excess Medical Deduction — actual verified expenses over $35/month for a member 60+ or disabled, OR the flat $165 Standard Medical Expense Deduction (SMED) for verified expenses between $35.01 and $200; medical marijuana explicitly non-allowable
Determining Monthly Medical Expenses — sets the $165 SMED figure, effective October 1, 2016

Resource Eligibility Standards — categorically eligible households are exempt from the resource test entirely; the $3,000 (standard) / $4,500 (60+ or disabled) resource limit applies only to Standard Eligibility households; sponsor-deeming and resource-transfer disqualification rules
Countable Resources — liquid vs. non-liquid resource valuation; jointly-owned and commingled-resource rules

Exempt Resources — all vehicles totally exempt regardless of type (4.410(A)); home and surrounding property; federally tax-preferred retirement accounts and tax-deferred education accounts named individually; income-producing property and vehicles

crs.note: Fraudulent acts — penalties, including the drug-related-felony SNAP disqualification: 2 years (first offense) or permanent (second offense), but ONLY when the conviction is directly related to using SNAP/food stamp benefits to purchase controlled substances and that misuse is part of the court's own findings
